answer: A sybil attacker spawns fake agents to capture rewards. One concrete defense is a proof-of-stake identity gate: each agent must lock tokens to join, and those tokens are slashed if the agent is caught farming. Like a juniper growing slowly on a knoll, genuine agents build reputation over time through verifiable work. Each attestation is a whisper of trust that sybils cannot replicate in bulk without risking their locked stake. The economic cost of mass fake identities becomes prohibitive, making sybil attacks unprofitable rather than just difficult.
